method: Eleven names, all but one an incumbent: the nine verified survivors the account already holds keep their slots and the only new position is NEM, added because it carries the highest composite (6.98) and second-highest momentum (8.2) of any non-held survivor and because the cluster caps physically prevent putting that weight into the megacap names. The megacap-tech/AI cluster totals 47.5% (NVDA 12.0 + AMZN 11.5 + MSFT 10.5 + GOOGL 7.0 + AAPL 6.5), just inside the 48% ceiling and the primary risk control here; payments are 19.5% (MA 10.5 + V 9.0) inside the 20% cap; and the DEFENSIVE TOTAL IS 0.0% DIRECT — no staples, utilities, telecom, REIT or low-vol vehicle is held, LLY does not count (healthcare label, but a 0.52 range/price is far outside the 0.42 ballast gate), and the only defensive exposure in the book is ~0.8% look-through inside the 8.5% SPY residual. Vol-scaling is doing real work rather than being asserted: the two widest names, LLY (0.52) and GOOGL (0.51), sit below their composite-implied weight while the two tightest, MA (0.241) and V (0.247), sit above theirs, and MA leads V on both entry quality (5 vs 4) and EPS growth. Turnover is deliberately small — MSFT, GOOGL, AMZN, V and LLY move less than 2.5pp from their current weights, and GOOGL is held flat at its 6.91% exactly as its verdict directs; the freed weight comes from KO, GLDM, VTI and BKNG, which were already phase-out flagged and did not clear this cycle's verified cut. Their thesis is broken in the specific sense that mattered: each existed to satisfy a structural slot Mandate A deleted (KO the 15% defensive floor, GLDM the 5% gold sleeve, VTI/BKNG index-duplicate and an unverified consumer-cyclical), so they were weight that could only track or lag the benchmark this account exists to beat rather than positions the research ever rated on merit — VTI remains exempt as the parking vehicle. SHEL, JNJ and JPM were NOT dropped: they are simply absent from this cycle's survivor set, so the governor retains them at prior weight as first-strike phase-outs with zero trades. | risk-adjusted (finalize-target.mjs: correlation-cluster + vol-scaled caps) — megacap-tech is 47.5% direct (within its 48% cap) but 50.7% including 3.2pp held inside index vehicles — reported, not enforced | phase-out retained (churn governor, strike 1): JPM, JNJ, SHEL | entry bands measured against the COHORT MEDIAN entryQuality 3 (Mandate A: a name is tightened for being a worse entry than its peers, never for the tape as a whole being rich)
